resources.string: This mode will be available in an upcoming update.
Audio files will be added in a later update. Your choices are saved already.
Logic Mix is a logic puzzle game with levels, XP and daily challenges.
No XP: this task was already solved.
You have solved every number sequence in this pack. New tasks will come in updates.
Drag a finger across neighbouring letters. Diagonals are not allowed.
You have finished every word search level for this language. New levels will come in updates.
Choose how you want to train your logic. You can change this later in Settings.
Dynamic mixed puzzle gameplay with streaks, bonus rewards, and a faster pace.
A personalized logic workout using the categories you select, at a comfortable pace.
Play one selected puzzle category independently.
Select one or more categories for your personal workout.
Select the category you want to play first. All other categories stay available.
Arcade style is saved. It will mix puzzles from all categories once the mixed mode is ready.
Your training categories are saved. The mix will be built from them once the mixed mode is ready.
All your entries and notes will be cleared.
Fix the equation: move exactly %1$d match(es). Drag a match to an empty spot.
Out of moves. Undo or reset.
The current game will be lost.
No move completes a line right now.
Move a ball along a free path. Line up 5 or more of the same color.
Your current progress will be reset.
Puzzles in your language are not ready yet, so English puzzles are shown.
Tap a cell or a clue to start.
Mini crosswords are not available in Chinese yet: they need a character-based grid and input.
Count the shapes in each cell.
Follow the turn from cell to cell.
Two things change at once: track each one separately.
Compare rows and columns: each direction has its own rule.
Find the tile that completes the grid.
Which shape is the original turned by the shown angle?
Which shape is the original after the shown flip?
Which figure has the shown silhouette?
Which shape is the same, only turned?
Which key fits the opening? Keys can be turned, not flipped.
Which fragment fills the missing part of the pattern?
Apply the steps in order. What do you get?
The folded paper is punched. What does it look like unfolded?
Which net folds into a cube?
Which figure is the result of the operation?
Which shape is different from the other three?
No moves available — the board was shuffled.
No chain is available right now.
Connect 2 or more dots of one color. Close a loop to clear that color.
Find the number that comes next in the sequence.
Calculate the value of the expression. Remember the order of operations.
Calculate the value of the expression. Pay attention to the brackets.
Choose the sign (+, −, × or ÷) that replaces the ? and makes the equation true.
Each number in the pyramid is the sum of the two numbers directly below it. Find the number that replaces the ?.
Each number in the pyramid is the sum of the two numbers directly below it. Find the number that replaces the ?. Empty cells (_) are unknown too, but you can work them out.
In every row of the table, the first two numbers produce the third one by the same hidden rule. Find the number that replaces the ?.
In every row, the first two numbers produce the third one by the same hidden rule. The columns follow this rule too: the top two numbers produce the bottom one. Find the number that replaces the ?.
Each symbol stands for a whole number from 1 to 20, the same everywhere. Use the equations to find the value of the last line (?).
Every number on the left is turned into the number on the right by the same hidden rule. Find the number that replaces the ?.
Add together all the numbers in the list that are multiples of %1$s.
Count how many numbers in the list are multiples of %1$s.
Find the difference between the largest and the smallest number in the list.
Count how many numbers in the list are greater than %1$s.
Add up all the digits of all the numbers in the list. For example, the number 47 gives 4 + 7.
Find the difference between the largest and the second largest number in the list.
The letters stand for the numbers given above. Replace each letter with its number and calculate the value of the expression.
Look at the difference between each number and the one before it.
Every step changes the number by the same amount: %1$s. Apply one more step to the last number.
Check whether each number is made from the previous one by multiplying.
Every number is the previous one multiplied by %1$s. Do one more multiplication.
The steps between neighbouring numbers are not all equal. Compare every second step.
The steps take turns: first %1$s, then %2$s, then %1$s again, and so on. Continue the pattern.
Write down the differences between neighbouring numbers, then look at how those differences change.
The differences themselves grow by %1$s each time. Work out the next difference, then add it to the last number.
Two sequences are mixed together. Look at the 1st, 3rd and 5th numbers separately from the 2nd, 4th and 6th.
Numbers in the 1st, 3rd, 5th… places change by %1$s each time; numbers in the 2nd, 4th, 6th… places change by %2$s. Continue the group that comes next.
Each number is made from the previous one using two operations in a row.
Multiply the previous number by %1$s, then add %2$s. Do this once more.
Multiply the previous number by %1$s, then subtract %2$s. Do this once more.
Take three numbers in a row. How is the third one related to the first two?
Each number is the sum of the two numbers before it. Add the last two numbers.
Two different operations take turns. Look at how you get from one number to the next, step by step.
The steps take turns: multiply by %1$s, then add %2$s, then multiply again, and so on. Continue the pattern.
Look for × and ÷ in the expression. They are calculated before + and −, even if they come later.
Begin with %1$s. Replace it with its result, then continue with the remaining operations.
Whatever is inside the brackets is calculated first.
Start with the brackets: %1$s. Then do × and ÷, and finish with + and −.
Put each sign (+, −, ×, ÷) in place of the ?, calculate, and compare the result with the number after the equals sign.
For example, with %1$s the left side would be %2$s, not %3$s. So that sign does not fit. Check the others.
Remember that × and ÷ are calculated before + and −. Check which sign makes the left side equal to the number on the right.
Start with the two cells right below the ?.
Add those two numbers. You do not need any other cells.
One of those two cells is empty. Work backwards: a number in the pyramid minus one of the two cells below it gives the other one.
The ? is in the bottom row. Find a number above it that is built from the ? and a neighbouring cell.
Work backwards: that number minus the neighbouring cell gives the ?. If a cell you need is empty, find it first.
Study one complete row: what happens to the first two numbers to give the third?
Study one complete row or column: what happens to the first two numbers to give the third?
Try combining the first two numbers of a row with “%1$s”. Check this on the complete rows first.
Try combining the first two numbers of a row with “%1$s”, then adding %2$s to the result. Check this on the complete rows first.
Try combining the first two numbers of a row with “%1$s”, then subtracting %2$s from the result. Check this on the complete rows first.
Only one symbol is used. Ask yourself what number makes the first equation true.
If the symbol appears several times, its total is the number multiplied by how many times it appears. Take away the plain numbers first, then divide.
Look for the equation with the fewest different symbols. It is the easiest to start with.
Find the value of one symbol first, then put it into the other equations to find the next one. Finally work out the last line.
Put the pairs in order of the left number. Look at how much the right number changes when the left number grows by 1.
The right number grows by %1$s for each step of 1. Multiply the left number by %1$s, then check what must be added or subtracted.
Compare the pairs: the right number does not change by equal steps when the left number grows by 1.
Try multiplying the left number by itself, then check whether anything must be added or subtracted.
Try multiplying the left number by a number close to itself (a little bigger or smaller).
Go through the list and mark the numbers that are multiples of %1$s. Ignore all the others.
A number is a multiple of %1$s if dividing it by %1$s leaves no remainder. Add only the marked numbers.
A number is a multiple of %1$s if dividing it by %1$s leaves no remainder. Count the marked numbers; do not add them.
Find the largest and the smallest number in the list.
Subtract the smallest number from the largest one.
Go through the list and mark the numbers bigger than %1$s. A number equal to %1$s does not count.
Count the marked numbers. The answer is how many there are, not their sum.
Split every number into its separate digits.
Add all these digits together, one by one. A two-digit number gives two digits to add.
Find the largest number first, then the largest of the remaining ones.
Subtract the second largest number from the largest one.
Start by replacing every letter with its number.
Then calculate the brackets first, then × and ÷, and finally + and −.
Then calculate × and ÷ first, and finally + and −.
